outcome: duration of sensory and motor blockade
cohort: 80 women undergoing elective caesarean section under spinal anaesthesia
finding: Intravenous lidocaine given as a supplementary agent in patients undergoing cesarean section under spinal anesthesia prolonged the duration of the sensory and motor blockade of spinal anesthesia and delayed the first analgesic request by patients without hemodynamic disturbance, respiratory depression and compromising the fetus.
